clue.text: Hold up piece of ermine from judge's garment

indicators.note: a piece of a word here is just its opening letter, taken on its own

blocks.note: to hold up a bank or coach is to rob it
the first letter of ermine

explanation.surface: A thief snatches a scrap of fur trim from a judge's ceremonial gown.
explanation.walkthrough: Ermine fur really does trim judicial robes, which makes the surface feel like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Judges in court wear a long formal gown, which is called a robe.

clue.text: Sappers fought, we hear, in deserts

indicators.note: what we hear is the sound of the word, not its spelling, so a word for fought is replaced by one pronounced the same

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are nicknamed sappers
fought a war, said the same as a hospital ward

explanation.surface: Military engineers are said to have done battle out in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: Deserts is not sandy places but the word in 'just deserts', what someone deserves. RE, the Royal Engineers, are the British Army's sappers.
explanation.definitionFit: Your deserts are what you have earned or merited, good or bad, much like a prize earned.

clue.text: Concerns shown about boss, one in university department

indicators.note: a word placed about others wraps around them, so the concerns go on either side

blocks.note: concerns are firms or companies
a boss is a raised knob or stud, as on a shield
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Worries are voiced over the boss and a staff member in an academic faculty.
explanation.walkthrough: Boss reads as an employer, but here it is a decorative knob. Concerns are firms, and the inserted letters go just before the plural ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Business studies is an academic subject taught at colleges, so a department of that name exists at many universities.

clue.text: In which only brothers and sisters may be employed?

definitions.text: In which only brothers and sisters may be employed?

blocks.clueFragment: In which only brothers and sisters may be employed?
blocks.note: surface reading: a family firm that hires nobody but siblings
setter's reading: trade unionists call one another brother and sister, so this is a workplace open only to union members

explanation.walkthrough: Union members traditionally address each other as brother and sister, which turns the family business into a union-only workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed shop is a workplace where every employee must belong to a particular trade union.

clue.text: Hold out, then abandon final defensive position

blocks.note: to hold out is to endure or last
to ditch something is to abandon it

explanation.surface: Soldiers resist as long as they can, then give up their final stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A last ditch was literally the final trench defended in a battle, hence a desperate final stand.

clue.text: Dawn, star at university

blocks.note: the Sun is our nearest star
a student in residence at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: Dawn sounds like a woman's name, a star student at university.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge means being in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunup is the moment the sun rises, the start of the day, so it is another word for daybreak.

clue.text: Type of biscuit shown in compendium I have

blocks.note: a digest is a compilation or summary of material
the contraction I've

explanation.surface: Someone owns a reference book listing kinds of biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: A digestive is a plain semi-sweet wheatmeal biscuit, a British teatime staple.
explanation.definitionFit: The digestive is a well-known variety of plain wholemeal cookie eaten in Britain, so it is one kind of biscuit.

clue.text: Valets have first choice in service

indicators.note: a choice is a selection made freely, so the letters are picked into a new order of the setter's choosing

blocks.note: all fifteen letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: Manservants get first pick of something while serving their master.
explanation.walkthrough: Service reads as domestic work for valets, but it is a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvest festival is an annual church thanksgiving held in autumn, so it is a form of religious worship.

clue.text: American writer to attempt verse

blocks.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American author
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: An American author sets out to try writing verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Poe himself wrote famous poems such as The Raven, so the surface is true to life.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse and poetry both mean writing arranged in metrical lines rather than prose.

clue.text: Fellow to lubricate sword

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
to oil a part is to lubricate it

explanation.surface: A man is asked to grease a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A foil is a light blunt-tipped weapon used in fencing, so it is a kind of sword.

clue.text: Wife is at home nursing prisoners in a state

indicators.note: to nurse something is to hold it close in your arms, so the home word cradles the convicts

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for wife
taken as written
someone at home is in
cons are convicts

explanation.surface: A wife stays home caring for convicts somewhere in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisconsin is one of the fifty constituent members of the United States, in the Midwest.

clue.text: A shrub - gardener's first rambling rose

indicators.note: the first of the gardener means only that word's opening letter is wanted
a rambling plant sprawls in every direction, so these letters spread out of their order

blocks.note: the initial of gardener
the flower's letters, to be mixed

explanation.surface: A gardener's favourite plant is a rambling rose bush.
explanation.walkthrough: A rambling rose is a real climbing variety, so 'rambling' hides in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse is a spiny yellow-flowered evergreen bush of heaths, also called furze.

clue.text: Joint in road caused annoyance

indicators.note: one word sitting in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation for road
the ankle is a joint of the leg

explanation.surface: A twisted ankle on the road was a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankled left a lasting bitterness or irritation, which is causing annoyance.

clue.text: French chemist, super at developing

indicators.note: something developing changes shape as it grows, so these letters take a new form

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A French scientist is excellent at developing things, perhaps vaccines or photos.
explanation.walkthrough: Louis Pasteur did develop vaccines and pasteurisation, so 'developing' feels like praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the nineteenth-century French scientist behind germ theory and pasteurisation.

clue.text: Inadequate move involving rook gets summary treatment

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so the move word encloses the chess piece

blocks.note: short of what is needed
to shift is to move
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A weak chess move with a rook earns a curt dismissal.
explanation.walkthrough: Summary here means brief and without ceremony, as in summary justice.
explanation.definitionFit: Short shrift is curt, unsympathetic dealing; originally the brief confession allowed before execution.

clue.text: Dreadfully hot in French resort - that can make one vulnerable

indicators.note: something done dreadfully is done badly, so these letters fall out of order

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
Nice, the resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: The awful heat on the Riviera leaves a holidaymaker exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word placing the heat in Nice, but its letters belong to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on thin ice is in a precarious, risky position, liable to come to harm or fail.

clue.text: Broadcasting (on air), this student of the past

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters something widely, like seed sown by hand, so these letters are thrown about

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A scholar of history is presenting a programme live on air.
explanation.walkthrough: TV historians are familiar figures, so the broadcasting scene seems literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A historian studies and writes about earlier times and events, so is a scholar of bygone ages.

clue.text: Provide background, as one working with props might

definitions.text: as one working with props might

blocks.note: first meaning: describe the circumstances before telling a story

blocks.clueFragment: as one working with props might
blocks.note: second meaning, cryptic: a stagehand literally arranges the scenery for a play

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic hint at a theatre crew member dressing the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To set the scene is figuratively to give context in advance and literally to arrange stage scenery.

clue.text: Goods thrown into the sea from planes (American)

blocks.note: jets are aircraft
the usual abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: American aircraft drop cargo into the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is cargo deliberately cast overboard to lighten a ship, unlike flotsam which floats away from a wreck.

clue.text: Island produce initially eaten by boy

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
food eaten by someone ends up inside them, so the boy's name swallows the letter

blocks.note: a boy's name
the opening letter of produce

explanation.surface: A lad munches fresh produce from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Boy names in crosswords can be any male first name; here it is Cyrus.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus is a Mediterranean island nation south of Turkey.

clue.text: Use veil wilily, becoming hard to pin down

indicators.note: doing something wilily means cunningly and craftily, so these letters are slyly rearranged

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone cunningly wears a veil to avoid being identified.
explanation.definitionFit: Elusive describes something difficult to catch, find or define precisely.

clue.text: Crept from border with daughter

blocks.note: an edge is a border
the usual abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone sneaked away from a frontier with their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge somewhere is to move slowly and carefully, inching forward much as one creeps.

clue.text: Show more stamina than others abroad on holiday?

blocks.note: someone abroad is out of the country
a holiday visit is a stay

explanation.surface: A tourist abroad lingers longer than everyone else on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: To outstay is to stay longer than others, here framed as endurance.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstay others is to remain longer than they do, which shows greater staying power.

clue.text: Upset, set off in street clothes

indicators.note: one word placed in another goes inside it
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation for street
to set off is to go

explanation.surface: Someone upset storms out in their street wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'street clothes' looks like one phrase, but street is wordplay and clothes alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Togs is an informal word for garments, outfits one wears.

clue.text: Second chapter provided one example of literature

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
C is the abbreviation for chapter
provided that means if
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A second chapter supplied an instance of a literary work.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction is a genre of writing, so a sci-fi novel is one kind of literary work.

clue.text: Discussing a beating

blocks.note: first meaning: examining or reviewing something in detail
second meaning: a thrashing, as in giving someone a ...

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a verb phrase, the second a noun phrase; the same words serve both.
explanation.definitionFit: Going over a topic means reviewing it in detail, and a going-over is slang for a violent thrashing.

clue.text: Girl, failing to finish in front, is pointing in the wrong direction

indicators.note: a word that fails to finish stops short, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a miss is a young girl
someone in front of the field is leading

explanation.surface: A girl who doesn't win the race despite leading points runners the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something misleading gives a false impression, sending people astray as a wrong signpost would.

clue.text: An advantage being rich? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means not the whole word, so its last letter is removed

blocks.note: plush means luxurious and rich

explanation.surface: Is wealth really an advantage? Only partly, the clue suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is a benefit or positive factor, as in pluses and minuses.
